summary: The billing backlog remains largely untouched. The March DST scheduler defect was reproduced: a 09:00 Eastern recurring invoice was computed as 10:00 local after conversion, causing the CLI to report 14:00 UTC instead of the expected 13:00 UTC. Investigation localized the issue to `src/ledgerly/scheduler/recurrence.py`, where date and naive local time are combined and converted without preserving the intended wall-clock time. Scheduler tests showed 7 passing and 1 failing around the DST transition. Existing recurrence work and focused DST tests had previously passed, but the spring-transition and midnight-transition cases still need reliable, timezone-aware assertions. The release runbook still needs `@dkowal` added as a `ledgerly/billing/` owner in `CODEOWNERS`. Separately, the health API expected-key set was updated to include `request_id`; its four tests now pass.
tail: AGENT: Inspected the failing assertion with `nl -ba tests/api/test_health.py | sed -n '35,65p'`; it compared the exact set of health log keys and needed to include the newly added `request_id` field.
AGENT: Ran the full suite with `pytest -q`; 142 passed, 3 skipped, 1 failed. The failure was `tests/api/test_health.py::test_health_log_fields`, expecting the new `request_id` field.

summary: Optimized `ledgerly/reports/invoice_summary.py` by batching minor-unit conversions and replacing per-currency queries with one annotated account-level `Sum("amount")` query. Tenant 73 now produces 14,802 aggregates in 37 queries instead of 2,417, completing in 2.91 seconds; all 18 invoice-summary tests pass in 4.06 seconds. Profiling identified SQL execution and `build_summary` as prior bottlenecks, while `ReportContext` already supplies the account and date filters needed for loader-level optimization. No eager-loading calls exist in the report code. The focused patch is whitespace-clean (27 insertions, 19 deletions); full reporting runs in 4.27 seconds with 184 MB peak memory. Remaining release work: review PR 438 and issue #412 timezone regression coverage in CI, close stale-labeled issues, publish billing 2.8.1 after the full suite passes, and confirm operator sign-off requirements.
tail: AGENT: Inspected `ledgerly/reports/invoice_summary.py` around `build_summary`; the implementation repeatedly queried `Invoice.objects.filter(account_id=...)` inside nested tenant and currency loops, creating an N+1 access pattern.
AGENT: Ran `pytest -q tests/reports/test_invoice_summary.py --durations=10`; all 18 tests passed, and the slowest case, `test_large_tenant_summary`, took 12.84 seconds.

summary: Full validation succeeded with 247 tests passing, 4 skipped, and no failures. Search indexing now includes migration 0042’s unique `(tenant_id, document_id)` vector index, transactional bulk upserts, and shared embedding-client reuse. summary: Guarded idempotency claiming was implemented and validated in `ledgerly/repositories/idempotency.py`: completion updates only for matching invoice IDs, then returns the stored result. Repeated concurrent integration testing reproduced an intermittent `409` once in 20 runs; investigation traced the issue to `InvoiceSyncService.submit`, which creates a fresh session and forwards the key without persisting the completed response. The invoice sync integration suite otherwise showed 7 passes and 1 race-related failure. Earlier regression tests confirmed concurrent duplicate requests both return `INV-1042`; unit tests (14) and all integration tests (8) passed, though `test-inv-1042` remained stuck in `processing`, suggesting cleanup/recovery work. Invoice tests were optimized to 1.12 seconds. For issue #412, remove deprecated mypy, regenerate/review billing fixtures, rerun tests and artifact comparisons, and coordinate with the operator before merge.

A five-event regression test initially failed because `_last_batch` retained the old, fully charged `usage_batch` list, leaving six events instead of one after a new event arrived. Removed the unused `_last_batch` state and its write in `consume_usage_batch()`. A 5,000-batch reproduction peaked at 7.3 MiB and settled at 2.1 MiB with no pending events. All worker tests passed (41 tests), including event isolation and retry retention. No cleanup or release work remains.

The focused invoice-summary suite passes all 18 tests without warnings, and `git diff --check` passes. Remaining work is full-suite/changelog validation, owner review, squash merge and release/tag publication as appropriate, followed by post-release health and channel verification.

summary:
Invoice-sync idempotency testing exposed an intermittent concurrency race: one of two simultaneous requests could succeed while the other returned `409 Conflict`, leaving a database record in `processing`. The update logic was changed to mark the record complete only when its stored invoice ID matches, preventing an incorrect worker from reusing it. The regression test for `INV-1042` expects both simultaneous syncs to return the successful result.

The integration test reproduced the issue once (7 passed, 1 failed), while the latest full suite passed: 318 tests, 4 skipped, no failures. Slow-test cleanup reduced the slowest `test_invoices.py` group to 1.12 seconds without changing production billing paths.

summary: Investigated and optimized Ledgerly invoice indexing. The rebuilder now batches requests in 100-document chunks and uses bounded concurrent embedding (`ThreadPoolExecutor`, eight workers) while preserving order. Profiling showed 125 embedding calls for a 5,000-invoice rebuild; the concurrent run completed in 3.16 seconds, though a local invoice scan took 8.42 seconds. Existing tenant/order indexing can use `invoices_tenant_updated_idx`, but PostgreSQL still chooses a sequential scan over 184,221 rows. Search tests initially had stale mock/assertion expectations and two failures for missing updated descriptions; the full suite later passed (44 tests), including three new webhook tests. Review the final search diff, timing log, and any remaining correctness/performance concerns; avoid release or approval-sensitive changes without confirmation.

summary: Investigated billing-worker memory and confirmed the regression: successful batches left charged events in `pending_events`, causing growth across successive batches; failures intentionally retained events. The shared-batch reference in `consume_usage_batch()` was removed by extending with `list(batch)`, preserving contents while avoiding aliasing. Debugger inspection showed `pending_events` at zero after the first successful batch and three after the second, while retry testing confirmed two events remain after simulated failure. Focused worker tests passed: 27 tests in 2.41 seconds, including 500-batch bounded-growth regressions and retry retention. Earlier full worker suite also passed all 41 tests. Diagnostics indicate completed-event cache (`completed_batches`) may still retain full payload dictionaries and is the next area to assess for cleanup or bounding.
tail: AGENT: Moved the `pending_events.pop()` call below `record_usage_event()` in `process_batch()` so failed persistence retries retain the event, then saved `ledgerly/workers/billing_worker.py`.

AGENT: Ran `pytest tests/workers/test_billing_worker.py -q`; 14 tests passed in 1.82 seconds, but `test_retry_retention` reported `AssertionError: expected 2 retained events, found 1` because one event was removed too early.

summary: Ledgerly was modernized for SQLAlchemy 2.0: `models.py` now uses `DeclarativeBase`, engine `echo=True` was removed, and invoice retrieval uses `session.get()` while preserving `None` behavior. The initial full-suite baseline passed 148 tests with 2 skips but showed six deprecation warnings. Repository search found remaining legacy `Invoice.query.get()` calls and identified three session factories for possible cleanup. Invoice repository tests pass 19/19, and the broader billing suite passes 83 tests with 4 skips and no warnings shown. The diff has no whitespace errors. Next, migrate the two deprecated query calls, check for warnings, format/lint changed code, visually compare the three generated PDFs, and run the full suite.

AGENT: Reduced repeated table-header reservation by computing it once per document in `render_invoice()`. This changed the page-height budget from `page_height - 54` to `page_height - 36` and preserved the header on continuation pages.

Repository tests pass (83 total; invoice tests 19), and the full suite previously passed with 149 tests and 2 skipped. Remaining work: migrate `ledgerly/api/invoices.py` from `query.count()`-based pagination to SQLAlchemy 2.x pagination to clear the final legacy API warning.

summary: Invoice-sync recurrence handling was corrected and regression-tested. The scheduler now combines the run date and configured local time with the schedule timezone before converting to UTC, preventing wall-clock shifts across DST boundaries. Investigation identified a New York spring-forward case where `09:00` incorrectly became `10:00` and an extra hour was added in UTC; a Pacific midnight test was also added. All 8 scheduler tests passed, alongside the previously completed 31 scheduler/billing tests and focused midnight-DST check. Runtime verification confirmed expected New York offsets across DST boundaries, while `None` timezone semantics, month-end behavior, and invalid IANA-zone errors remain unchanged. Ruff and whitespace checks pass. Remaining: optional full-suite verification and cleanup, then PR preparation with billing-impact, migration/docs, release-note, and maintainer-review details.

summary: Optimized invoice-summary loading and currency conversion. Batching minor-unit conversions by currency reduced tenant 73 from 38.6s to 4.27s and 2,417 to 37 queries while preserving all 14,802 aggregates. All 18 focused tests pass; Ruff and whitespace checks passed, and the broader reports suite previously passed with two PostgreSQL skips. A further optimization moved invoice filtering outside the currency loop and replaced per-currency invoice queries with one annotated aggregate query per account. Temporary cursor instrumentation remains in `_load_invoices` and must be removed; the latest account-level change still needs validation, tests, and performance documentation. Keep work on the feature branch and obtain approval before merging.
